allies.rationale_text: Authenticity helps non-violent-communication surface real experience and tension instead of keeping the exchange in impression-management mode.
allies.source_quote: being authentic with this person now
allies.affinity_rationale: Radical Transparency/Truth 'aligns perfectly with the model's focus on honesty in communication' — authenticity provides the disposition that makes non-violent communication genuine rather than manipulative.
allies.activation_condition: When communication requires genuine honesty about needs and observations rather than strategic impression management or diplomatic avoidance

allies.rationale_text: Critical-thinking helps non-violent-communication stress-test claims while still protecting the relationship enough for synthesis.
allies.source_quote: This model necessitates critical thinking to challenge assumptions and uncover truth.
allies.affinity_rationale: NVC 'necessitates critical thinking to challenge assumptions and uncover truth' — the Socratic Method provides the discipline for stress-testing assertions and identifying logical gaps.
allies.activation_condition: When communication breakdown stems from untested assumptions about the other party's motives rather than verified understanding through structured questioning

antagonists.rationale_text: Authority-bias undermines non-violent-communication when role power suppresses direct observation-and-needs exchange.
antagonists.source_quote: non-violent-communication conflicts with authority-bias (authority bias) when role power suppresses direct needs-and-observations exchange.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Role power suppresses direct needs-and-observations exchange — authority bias causes lower-power participants to withhold authentic communication to avoid challenging hierarchical expectations.
antagonists.activation_condition: When power dynamics prevent the open, bidirectional needs-and-observations exchange that non-violent communication requires

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias blocks non-violent-communication when people cling to their interpretation instead of staying open to revision.
antagonists.source_quote: non-violent-communication conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when rigid adherence to one's own interpretation blocks the open, non-judgmental listening that the model requires.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Rigid adherence to one's own interpretation blocks the open, non-judgmental listening the model requires — confirmation bias filters incoming communication through existing beliefs.
antagonists.activation_condition: When one party's rigid interpretation of the other's motives prevents genuine listening and causes communication to devolve into defensive pattern-matching
